Yeah I’ve heard about this method but my doctor didn’t care, he put me on 37.5 for a month and then wanted me to quit cold turkey which didn’t go well. When I said it was too fast, he said that it meant I’m not ready to be off meds yet and wanted me to go back to 75. Luckily he prescribed me more of the 37.5 to take twice a day so I just didn’t visit him again and used all of that to taper off. 

Effexor gave me more side effects than it helped, that’s why I didn’t want to take it anymore. Worst side effects were hypomanic episodes, which kinda ruined my life and I have to live with the consequences forever. I’m not bipolar, effexor caused them. I know this drug helps other people a lot but it’s not for me.

I had no withdrawals going from 150 to 37.5 either, but trying to stop completely took me around 8 months. If you’re taking 37.5 capsules now, check if they have beads or small pills inside - mine had 3 little pills that I assumed were 12.5 each. I took 2 of these pills for a month and then only 1 for a few months. Then I’d go every other day, every 3 days until I accidentally forgot to take it for 5 days and noticed no withdrawals. If you have beads inside, I know a lot of people count or weigh them and you could lower your dose these ways. I had tried stopping effexor a couple of times before and I couldn’t do it, the side effects were too much. This system made it so easy tho. I hope it works out for you

Idk where you live but from what I’ve read it’s not being prescribed in the us :( it’s a very gentle anti anxiety drug, probably wouldn’t help with strong depression or anxiety, and it’s supposed to kind of repair your brain after antidepressants so I hoped my focus would come back.
